threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the High Road' instead of just 'the road' when talking about Lea Bridge. Only locals know it’s a vibe, not just a route.
Saw a bloke on the 3 bus serenading the driver with a ukulele. Driver just shook his head, but it made the whole ride feel like a scene from a film.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy selling homemade falafel from his bike, while the Turkish grandmas argued over who makes it best at the market.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you'll find old-school Kiosk owners who know your name and what you usually buy—where else can you get a personal touch with your 5€ beer?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Real locals know to carry a reusable bag at all times. Tourists scramble to buy overpriced ones at the corner store when they hit the farmers market.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a man in a full tuxedo boarding the 21 Hayes—just another Tuesday in the Tenderloin, I guess. The city knows how to keep things interesting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all Gràcia bars serve tapas, but many just vibe with vermut and unpretentious pintxos. The locals know where to find the real gems.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still avoid talking to the elderly in the park, too caught up in their phones and maps.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'overground' when you hop on at London Fields. Locals know it’s just the quick route.
Heard a lad on the 196 confess he’s never been to the Brixton Windmill, swearing he’ll go next weekend. Good luck with that!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a grumpy old man feeding pigeons while chatting with a breakdancer in the park. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24-hour Döner place that serves breakfast burritos with curry sauce. You won't find that combo anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can effortlessly navigate BART delays while non-locals just stare at their phones, waiting for updates that never come.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 14 Mission, casually scrolling his phone. Only in SF would you dress to the nines for a Friday night out but still ride the bus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all love 'aqua de Valencia.' Most of us prefer a simple vermut with olives at midday, way more authentic.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll spot them by their hesitant approach to the metro. They often miss the right exit because they're too busy scanning their maps instead of the signs.
